summary: Follow-up on the 2026-02-27 outage affecting Solaris Health inference endpoints. Discussed root cause (KV cache eviction + aggressive client timeouts), mitigations (timeout bump, cache pinning, autoscaling knobs), and next steps for canary and Dedicated capacity evaluation.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-18 14:30 UTC | Duration: 55 minutes | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marta (Solaris Head of MLOps), Ethan (Solaris SRE), Naomi (Solaris CTO)

Summary: quick postmortem review, confirm mitigations, align on canary and reliability items, and next steps to prevent recurrence.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, apologies for the slight delay, call recorded. Quick round of intros?
[00:18] Marta: Marta here — we had a pretty rough week end of feb, wanted to make sure we got a concrete plan.
[00:25] Naomi: Naomi, CTO, I'm mostly here to understand risk and the timeline for fixes.
[00:33] Ethan: Ethan, SRE, I'll share the logs and the flamegraphs after.
[00:40] Priya: Priya from Redwood, I'll lead the technical mitigation and patch work.
[01:05] Jordan: Cool, so short context — on 2026-02-27 you saw increased 5xxs and tail latency spikes for the prod chat endpoints, correct?
[01:18] Marta: Yeah, we saw a cascade: throughput dropped, autoscaler didn't spin up fast enough and then several requests timed out client-side which amplified retries.
[01:30] Priya: From Redwood's traces we saw simultaneous KV cache eviction events and heavy checkpointing on the host that coincided with GC spikes on the customer's side — or that's what the samples show, transcription sometimes mislabels GC but it's more like process memory reclaim.
[01:50] Ethan: Right, and our initial look shows the client timeouts are 2.5s, which is aggressive for long-context chats, particularly when a new KV-page is required and quantized model cold-starts happen.
[02:05] Jordan: So two axes: server-side cache pressure and client timeout/retry policy. Also capacity — you were on shared hosted plans, correct?
[02:16] Marta: Hosted API tier, yes. We were considering Dedicated but hadn't decided.
[02:25] Priya: Tech note: the root cause seems to be combined — when the KV cache evicted key segments, requests required repeated KV warmups and the inference runtime fell back to a slower code path, raising per-token latency. With client retries at 2.5s and our default retry backoff, you ended up with request storms.
[02:55] Ethan: There's also a small bug in our request batching that made some requests go to a lower-priority queue, so they didn't benefit from autoscaling quick path.
[03:10] Marta: OK so what's the immediate mitigation? We need something low-risk.
[03:20] Priya: Short term: bump client timeout to 10s for chat endpoints, disable aggressive client-side retries, and pin critical prefixes in KV cache for the hot routes. Also we'll push a server patch that changes the cache eviction heuristic to prefer TTL over LRU in low-memory situations.
[03:46] Naomi: Any danger to increasing timeouts? We worry about request pile-up.
[03:52] Priya: Valid. That's why we'll also coordinate autoscaler policy changes — lower scale-up threshold and faster warm pools in Dedicated or reserved mode. For hosted customers, Redwood can provide faster burst capacity but it's not infinite; for Dedicated you'd get more predictable throughput.
[04:10] Jordan: We proposed a quick canary: 10% of traffic routed to a path with timeout=10s, cache pinning enabled, and new eviction heuristic. Monitor error rate and tail latency for 48 hours. If stable, roll to 100%.
[04:28] Marta: That sounds reasonable, we also want a 24h canary before we change client-side defaults.
[04:35] Ethan: I'll need the config diffs and the exact log keys to watch.
[04:40] Priya: We'll share a runbook.
[04:45] [05:00] Jordan: On the audit/security front — Solaris asked for KMS/HSM details and SOC2 artifacts during the SLA talks. Naomi, you said you wanted them?
[05:10] Naomi: Yes, we need KMS integration proof for encryption at rest, RBAC audit logs, and network isolation details — especially if we move to Dedicated or Private.
[05:22] Priya: We'll attach the SOC 2 report and a KMS integration guide. For Private deployments we have an optional customer-managed KMS flow and HSM connectors.
[05:35] Marta: Great. Back to root cause — can you explain why eviction happened? Were you running a lot of models?
[05:42] Priya: The eviction triggers were due to a combination of model size, high fan-out of concurrent sessions, and some long sequences that bled into memory. Our runtime also performed a maintenance sweep that temporarily increased memory pressure. That sweep is on our radar to soften.
[06:05] Ethan: The maintenance sweep — is that something we can control or toggle per-tenant?
[06:10] Priya: We can expose a parameter to delay sweeps during peak traffic windows and we can reduce aggressiveness.
[06:18] Jordan: There's also the option of Dedicated capacity which prevents noisy neighbor effects; with reserved GPUs you get predictable KV capacities and faster autoscale warm pools.
[06:30] Marta: Cost is a factor; need to know ballpark committed monthly.
[06:36] Jordan: I'll follow up with a pricing sheet for 3 tiers of Dedicated (small/medium/large) and predicted per-token delta versus hosted with the new caching config.
[06:48] [10:00] Marta: We also had a question about model fallbacks. When a high latency occurs does Redwood automatically fall back to smaller model variants?
[10:10] Priya: We have a routing policy capability; we can configure a latency-based fallback to a smaller model or quantized variant. That can be part of the canary policy. Caveat: you may see quality drift and we recommend guardrail evals.
[10:30] Ethan: For the incident we saw, there were also spikes in upstream database calls which increased end-to-end latency, not just inference.
[10:40] Naomi: So multiple contributing factors.
[10:45] Priya: Exactly — we documented a causal chain: DB slow -> request queues -> heavier fan-out -> KV evictions -> slow inference path -> client retries -> amplification. We'll send the chain in the postmortem doc.
[11:05] Jordan: Any blockers for the canary?
[11:10] Ethan: Need logs and config we discussed, and internal approval for changing client timeouts.
[11:15] Marta: I'll check with product to approve timeout bump for user-facing services.
[11:20] Priya: We'll prepare a patch and a config diff; it's low risk and non-breaking. We'll also prepare an automated rollback if error rates increase.
[11:35] [20:00] Jordan: A quick note on observability — we'll add token-level cost and latency breakdown for your top 10 routes so you can see unit economics impact of canary and Dedicated.
[20:15] Marta: Good, that helps budget conversations.
[20:22] Naomi: Also share a performance regression alert tied to a small eval set so we catch quality drop if a fallback happens.
[20:30] Priya: We'll bundle that in the roll-forward plan.
[20:45] Ethan: On data residency and compliance — if we move Dedicated with a VPC option, does Redwood support customer-managed key rotation?
[20:55] Priya: Yes, KMS integration supports rotation and we can present HSM options for Private installs; we'll share the integration notes.
[21:10] Jordan: Recap of decisions: 1) Immediate canary with timeout bump and cache pinning 2) Redwood to ship eviction-heuristic patch 3) Solaris to review client retry policy and approve 24h canary 4) Redwood to share SOC2/KMS docs and Dedicated pricing.
[21:36] Marta: Sounds right. One more ask: can you simulate the incident for us? A replay or synthetic load test?
[21:44] Priya: We can run a replay on a staging cluster with your sample traffic traces. We'll coordinate with Ethan on data redaction.
[21:55] Ethan: I'll prepare traces and scrub PII.
[22:05] Jordan: Great. Any final questions?
[22:10] Naomi: Timeline — when can we expect the patch?
[22:15] Priya: We'll aim to deliver patch and config diffs by 2026-03-20 and a patched canary by 2026-03-22.
[22:25] Jordan: Alright, thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with artifacts, runbook, and the pricing sheet.
[22:35] Marta: Thanks, appreciate the fast turnaround.

End of transcript.
